summary: Lancelot Wilkinson (1805–1841) was an Indologist who studied at the East India Company College (~1821–1823). He held a post with the Bombay Civil Service from 1822 and taught Bapu Deva Sastri, Subaji Bapu, and Omkar Bhatt.
Lang Chen works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at Yale University, studying under doctoral supervisors Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff as well as teacher Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She pursued doctoral studies at Temple University under supervisor Charles Wei-hsun Fu, also studying under Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.

Langdon Warner (1881–1955) was an art historian and East Asian specialist who studied at Harvard (A.B. ~1899–1903). He directed the Pennsylvania Museum of Art (1917–1923) and served as a lecturer and fellow at Harvard and the Fogg Art Museum (1923–1950).

Lara Braitstein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and became Associate Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism there (attested 2026).

Larry DeVries is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Minnesota. He taught at Minnesota, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the University of Washington, and was affiliated with Langara College (attested 2005).

Lars Edman (1824–1921) was a Swedish linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at Uppsala University (1847–1857). He served at Uppsala as Docent in Oriental languages (1857) and later as Associate Professor of German and English (1863–1892).

Lars Fogelin is an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Michigan (1995–2003) under Carla Sinopoli. He has held positions at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.

Lars Martin Fosse (born 1950) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Oslo, Heidelberg University, and the University of Bonn. He is attested as a teacher at the University of Oslo in 2002.

Lars Nannestad Boisen (1803–1875) was a Danish linguist and Indologist who studied at Copenhagen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Bonn. His teachers included Georg Freytag, August Wilhelm von Schlegel, Christian Lassen, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Antoine-Léonard Chézy.

Lata Chhatre is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Her career includes positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University as Reader in the Department of Philosophy (attested 2009) and as Visiting Faculty (attested 2026).

Lata Deokar is an Indologist and Tibetologist who earned her MA and PhD from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth. She worked on the dictionary at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2000–2012) and was Visiting Faculty at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2026).

Lati Rinpoche (1922–2010) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery (Geshe Lharampa) and Gyuto Monastery. He was Abbot of Ganden Shartse Monastery (~1976–1984) and a Visiting Scholar at the University of Virginia (1976).

Latika Lahiri (born 1923) is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji in 1958 as an Indian Government scholar and held a post at the University of Delhi.

Laura Harrington is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who studied at Columbia University. Her teachers included Ryuichi Abe, Theodore Riccardi Jr., Gary A. Tubb, and Lozang Jamspal, among others.

Laura Massetti is a linguist and Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Cologne (2012–2016). She held research posts at Copenhagen, Oxford, and the Center for Hellenic Studies before becoming a researcher at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (2022–2025).

Lauran R. Hartley is a Tibetologist who has served as Adjunct Assistant Professor and Director of the Modern Tibetan Studies Program at Columbia University (attested 2026). She also held appointments at Indiana University Bloomington and Rutgers University.

Laurence Austine Waddell (1854–1938) was a Tibetologist and medical officer who graduated from the University of Glasgow (1878). He served in the Indian Medical Service (~1880–1917) and later became Professor of Tibetan at University College London (1906–1908).

Laurence Binyon (1869–1943) was an art historian and East Asian specialist who studied at Trinity College, Oxford. He was Keeper of Oriental Prints and Drawings at the British Museum (1915–1933) and held visiting professorships at Harvard and the University of Athens.

Laurence Khantipalo Mills (1932–2021) was a Buddhist studies practitioner and teacher. He studied under Acharya Buddharakkhita, Sangharakshita, Chien Ming Chen, and Dhardo Rinpoche, and served as the abbot of Wat Buddha Dhamma in 1978.
